Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Update an existing record and reflect the new state visibly in the interface.

The key idea for this feature is Record updates and state feedback.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
UpdateChanging an existing stored record.
Status fieldThe value that shows whether work is complete.
PersistenceA change that stays after refresh.
UI feedbackVisible evidence that the new state was applied.

Why the client needs this

  • Managers need to see whether work has been completed. This feature makes that status change real.
  • A visible completed state must match stored data, not just temporary styling.

Bring this forward from earlier pages

  • Return to the success criteria about reliable status changes.
  • Update the test plan with a check that still passes after refresh.

State-change habit

  • A style change in the DOM is not enough.
  • The backend must store the new status.
  • Refreshing the page is the simplest proof that the update persisted.

Completion state preview

A good completion feature changes both the stored data and the visible status.

Prepare report completed Saved

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • A status change is only complete when the stored value and the visible state both update.
  • The design should make completed work readable without making the interface noisy.
  • Use this feature to reinforce the idea that UI state should reflect stored data.

Generic update-request pattern

fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ status: "complete" })
});
PATCH

PATCH is used when you are changing part of an existing record.

status

Send only the value the backend actually needs to update.

JSON body

Even a small update still needs the data packaged clearly.

persistence

A true update survives refresh because the stored data changed, not just the styling.

Build it in this order

The completed state should be visible and persistent. If either part is missing, the feature is unfinished.

Step 1 static/js/app.js

Attach the completion action to each task row

  • Give every row a control that targets the correct task id.
  • Send an update request rather than faking the status in the DOM.
Step 2 app.py

Update the stored status

  • Receive the identifier and change only the intended record.
  • Persist the new status value in storage.
Step 3 Browser check

Redraw the list and prove persistence

  • Make the completed state easy to spot on screen.
  • Refresh and confirm the state survives because storage changed, not because of temporary styling.

Where the checks happen

HTML

The interface can require fields, constrain control types, and guide the user before submit.

JavaScript

The browser can check presence, shape, and request timing before sending data.

Flask

The backend must re-check the request because outside tools can bypass the browser entirely.

SQL / SQLite

Database rules keep the stored record sensible and consistent.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature

app.pyApplies the status changeUpdate the stored record and return a clear result

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • The status change targets the correct record.
  • The UI visibly distinguishes completed work.
  • The new state persists after refresh.
